claims.text: Controlled annealing of the as-cast refractory high-entropy alloy induces short-range chemical ordering.
Short-range chemical ordering enhances local lattice coherence.
Enhanced local lattice coherence strengthens electron–phonon interactions.
Stronger electron–phonon interactions facilitate Cooper-pair formation and the emergence of superconductivity.
The as-cast TaNbHfZrTi refractory high-entropy alloy has a fully disordered, random atomic distribution.
Rapid quenching after annealing freezes in the induced short-range chemical order.
Annealing produces both local chemical order and nanoscale clustering.
Short-range ordering lowers the energy barrier for Cooper-pair formation.
Annealed samples will exhibit a measurable superconducting transition.
Annealed samples will have a higher critical temperature than the as-cast baseline.
Annealed samples will have lower normal-state resistivity than the as-cast baseline.
Superconducting properties will be optimized within a particular annealing-temperature and annealing-time window.
Insufficient annealing will leave chemical ordering underdeveloped.
Excessive annealing can cause detrimental phase separation.
The untreated as-cast alloy is expected either to lack superconductivity or to have a substantially lower critical temperature because it lacks local chemical order.
The proposed comparison uses annealing at 600–800 °C for 1–10 hours and superconductivity measurements down to approximately 1 K.
Outside the proposed annealing window, mechanisms such as phase separation may dominate the superconducting response.
